mainEntity.name: How much does a BMW 7 Series 735i engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: For a BMW 735i, replacement costs vary by generation. E38 735i (M62B35) engines range from £800-£1,800 used, £1,800-£3,200 reconditioned, and £2,300-£4,200 rebuilt. E65 735i (N62B36A) engines range from £1,200-£2,500 used, £2,500-£4,200 reconditioned, and £3,500-£5,500 rebuilt. Labour adds approximately £800-£1,200 for specialist fitment.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of timing chain guide failure in a BMW 735i?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common telltale sign is a rattling noise from the engine on cold start, which may subside as oil pressure builds. You may also notice a check engine light, rough running, or plastic particles in the oil during a service. The M62 engine's plastic timing chain guides become brittle with age and typically fail between 80,000 and 100,000 miles.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a BMW 7 Series 735i?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on the car's condition and value. For an E38 735i worth under £2,500, consider repair or a used engine rather than a full rebuild. For cars worth £3,000-£5,000, a reconditioned or rebuilt engine typically justifies the premium via warranty and reliability. For E65 735is worth £4,000+, replacement cost is small relative to vehicle value. If the car is otherwise in excellent condition, a rebuilt engine with upgraded components can extend its life by 80,000+ miles.

mainEntity.name: How long does a BMW 7 Series 735i engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most BMW 735i engine replacements take 2-4 days for supply and fit at a specialist garage. The V8 engine's complexity - particularly on N62 units - means careful removal and installation is essential. Collection and delivery options are available nationwide, with most engines dispatched within 24-72 hours of order confirmation.

mainEntity.name: Do BMW 7 Series 735i replacement engines come with a warranty?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes - all rebuilt BMW 735i engines supplied through EnginesMarket include a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty. Used engines typically come with 3-6 month warranties, while reconditioned units usually include 6-12 month cover. Extended warranty options are available on most rebuilt units.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the M62 and N62 engines in the BMW 735i?

acceptedAnswer.text: The M62 is a 3.5-litre naturally aspirated V8 producing 235-238hp, fitted to E38 735is from 1996-2001. The N62 is a 3.6-litre naturally aspirated V8 producing 272hp, fitted to E65 735is from 2001-2005. The N62 produces significantly more power but is also more complex, with additional failure points including valve stem seals and cooling system issues not present on the M62.

historyTimeline.h2: BMW 7 Series 735i - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The BMW 735i debuted in the E38 generation in March 1996 as a V8-powered entry point above the six-cylinder 728i. It replaced the 730i's M60 3.0-litre V8 with a larger 3.5-litre M62 unit. The 735i name continued into the E65 generation with a 3.6-litre N62 V8 before being discontinued in 2005.

milestones.description: March 1996 - M62B35, 3.5L naturally aspirated V8, 235hp - launched in E38 735i
September 1998 - M62B35 (TU/updated), 3.5L V8, 238hp - E38 facelift with improved emissions and power
November 2001 - N62B36A, 3.6L naturally aspirated V8, 272hp - E65 735i launch

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the BMW 7 Series 735i is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h2: BMW 7 Series 735i Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The BMW 735i's M62 and N62 V8 engines are generally robust, but age-related failures are common on higher-mileage examples. E38 735is (M62, 1996-2001) suffer primarily from timing chain guide failure and VANOS seal degradation, while E65 735is (N62, 2001-2005) add valve stem seal and cooling system issues to the list. Rebuilt engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing these original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Timing Chain Guide Failure - Why the BMW 7 Series 735i M62 Fails
problems.rootCause: The plastic timing chain guides become brittle with age and heat cycles, cracking and breaking. When guides fail, the timing chain can slip, causing catastrophic engine damage. Plastic debris also contaminates the oil system.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace timing chain guides, chain, tensioner, VANOS seals
repairOptions.longevity: Viable if caught early and engine otherwise sound
Recommended if chain has slipped or guides have failed catastrophically

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical E38 735i (1996-2001) is worth £1,500-£5,000, with many examples under £3,000. A typical E65 735i (2001-2005) is worth £2,000-£7,000. For E38 735is valued under £2,500, a used engine or guide replacement may be more sensible than a full rebuilt unit. For cars worth £3,000-£5,000, reconditioned/rebuilt replacement usually justifies the premium via warranty and reliability.
problems.recommendation: If your 735i has timing chain rattle but the engine has not jumped timing, guide replacement is a cost-effective fix. If the chain has slipped or broken, the engine has almost certainly sustained internal damage - a rebuilt engine is the only reliable solution.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt M62B35 BMW 7 Series 735i engine prices

problems.group: Valve Stem Seal Failure & Oil Consumption
problems.h4: Valve Stem Seal Failure & Oil Consumption - BMW 7 Series 735i N62 Engine
problems.rootCause: The rubber valve stem seals harden and crack with age and heat exposure, losing their ability to seal the valve guide. Oil seeps into the combustion chamber and burns, producing blue smoke from the exhaust, particularly on startup.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace all valve stem seals (labour-intensive; cylinder head access required)
repairOptions.longevity: Viable if engine otherwise healthy and car worth £3,000+
Best for higher-mileage units with multiple concurrent failures

problems.vehicleValueCheck: See above. For E65 735is, valve stem seal replacement is typically viable if the car is worth over £3,000.
problems.recommendation: If your N62 735i has blue smoke on startup but runs well otherwise, specialist valve stem seal replacement is a sensible investment. If the engine has high mileage and other issues (cooling system, timing chain wear), a rebuilt engine with upgraded components may be the better long-term choice.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt N62B36A BMW 7 Series 735i engine prices

problems.h4: VANOS Seal Failure - BMW 7 Series 735i M62 Engine
problems.rootCause: The VANOS (variable valve timing) system relies on rubber seals that degrade over time, causing loss of oil pressure and reduced performance at low RPM. Symptoms include rough idle, hesitation on acceleration, and reduced low-end torque.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace VANOS seals, often done alongside timing chain work
Supply & fit, includes new VANOS units and seals, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Recommended if engine has multiple issues

problems.recommendation: VANOS seal failure on its own is not catastrophic. If your M62 735i has VANOS symptoms but the timing chain is healthy, the seal replacement is a straightforward specialist job. If the car is having the timing chain guides done, it makes sense to do VANOS seals at the same time as the labour overlaps significantly.
